chapter: Early New Orleans bands and records
title: Records with Johnny Miller, the ship's engineer
summary: Johnny Miller, a ship's engineer and pianist, organized the Panama and Dipper Mouth session with Sidney Arodin and Chink Martin.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, well I heard Panama and the Dipper Mouth.
That's right. Have you worked with Johnny Miller? I never did know much about him.
Well Johnny Miller, he was an engineer on the ships.

Oh, very good engineer, yeah. And every now and then he'd make a trip on the ships and then he'd come back and he'd play piano for a while. Until he felt like he wanted to make another trip, then he'd go and make another trip. But he was a very good piano player.
He had the records. Very good. And he got the session. So we all made the records. Sidney Airdin, Joe Larcanna, I think it was Monk Hazel, Chink Martin.
So Johnny Miller didn't work regularly then I guess as a musician. I never did get to hear him or meet him.

No he'd do just like I said. He'd play the piano for a while and he'd get the urge to make a trip. He'd just take out his union card and get on a ship. And an engineer on a ship, Bill, they always make good money. See there's, in other words there's three of them. There's first, second, and third engineers on those ships. The big ocean going. Yes, yes. He'd become a lieutenant commander in the Coast Guard during the war because of being an engineer.
